title: Adaptive Windowed Sequence Sculptor with Kernel Cost Heuristics
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Goal: Reduce padded tokens and end-to-end latency variance for mixed-length prefill+decode workloads by applying a lightweight windowed bucketing layer that cooperates with the kernel-cost model.

Background: Our current microbatch shaping reduces padding by grouping similar sequence lengths, but we still see excess padding for workloads with multimodal length distributions (chat + short completions + long context). The serving runtime can further improve cost and latency by using a fast estimator of kernel execution cost (per-length, per-kernel variant) to guide how we slice sequences into buckets and when to prefer prefill-first vs decode-first packing. This ticket explores an "Adaptive Windowed Sequence Sculptor" that: (1) computes short-term sequence-length histograms in sliding windows, (2) uses kernel-cost heuristics to choose bucket boundaries and kernel variants (e.g., fused attention vs tiled attention path), and (3) biases prefill scheduling to reduce tail latency for decode requests with high inter-dependency on KV cache.

Proposed approach:
- Collect low-overhead telemetry: per-request seq_len, model_id, hardware_tag, observed kernel variant chosen, kernel_exec_ms (approx), and whether the request is prefill or decode. Aggregate into a sliding-window histogram (window size configurable: default 10s).
- Maintain a small kernel-cost table (learned offline + online smoothing) keyed by (model_family, kernel_variant, seq_len_bucket, hw_class) with expected tokens/sec. Use this to estimate cost of packing different groups.
- Windowed sculptor: given the histogram, run a lightweight optimizer that proposes bucket boundaries that minimize expected padded tokens * cost_per_token subject to a latency SLO constraint (latency penalty for enlarging buckets). The optimizer runs every window or when distribution drift exceeds threshold.
- Prefill/decode biasing: when a high-cost kernel variant is needed for long sequences, prefer to schedule steady prefill batches to amortize KV cache cost; for short-decode-heavy windows, coalesce decode-first microbatches. Use priority lanes to ensure decode tail latency for interactive clients remains within SLO.
- Kernel hints & fallback: expose chosen kernel_variant hints to the kernel selector so that placement and kernel selection can further optimize execution; ensure safe fallback to stable kernel on mismatch.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end measured padded-token reduction >= 18% for a mixed benchmark (20% short, 60% medium, 20% long) compared to baseline coalescer.
- P50 generation latency unchanged (<= +2%) and P95 tail reduced by at least 10% for interactive decode flows in the benchmark.
- No regressions on throughput tests for large-batch synthetic traffic.
- Feature toggle present and rollout plan documented; option to run in "observe-only" mode for 2 weeks before activation.

Telemetry & metrics: pad_tokens_per_request, avg_kernel_cost_per_token, scheduling_decisions_per_window, latency_p50/p95, routing_miss_rate (kernel_hint vs actual), and cost_delta_per_hour. Dashboard link: (confluence/dashboard placeholder).

Implementation plan:
1) Spike: implement windowed histogram + simple greedy bucketer offline (2w).
2) Integrate kernel-cost table and fast estimator (1w).
3) Implement sculptor in runtime scheduling plane with feature flag (2w).
4) Canary and observe-only rollout (2w).
5) Full rollout with auto-tuning thresholds (1w).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: inaccurate kernel-cost table leads to suboptimal bucketing. Mitigation: start with conservative smoothing and add safety margin; enable observe-only and A/B tests.
- Risk: added scheduler CPU overhead. Mitigation: keep optimizer lightweight (greedy quantile split) and cap runtime budget per window.
- Risk: cross-tenant fairness when aggressive packing benefits some tenants. Mitigation: include tenant-level cost weighting and allow per-tenant opt-out.

Rollout notes: will gate on runtime-1.20; add console switch under "Optimize -> Microbatch shaping"; document expected behavior with examples.
